summary: Implemented TemplateClauseLibraryPage and its five owned components (TemplatesTab, ClauseLibraryTab, TemplateEditor, ClauseEditor, VersionHistoryModal), wired to all twelve contracted endpoints via a new clausesService and an extended templatesService, backed by the templateLibrarySlice zustand store and twelve new hooks (useTemplates, useCreateTemplate, useUpdateTemplate, useDeactivateTemplate, useReactivateTemplate, useTemplateVersions and the clause equivalents). Covers blank-name validation with exact error copy, 150-char name limits, predefined-list-only merge field insertion into Template Body, predefined Clause/Template Category and Risk Level dropdowns, colour-coded Risk Level badges (green/amber/red), Mandatory checkbox with the lock-in warning banner, Draft-to-Active auto-transition display, Version History modal (Version Number/Changed By/Date Changed/Change Summary), Deactivate/Reactivate with a confirm step, role-gated screen access (Tenant Admin/Legal Reviewer only) with an in-place permission-denied message for every other role, and role-gated Deactivate/Reactivate visibility (Tenant Admin only). Routed at /settings/template-clause-library in App.jsx. Lint and build are clean; all 25 tests pass (6 new for this screen). Screenshot comparison against IMG-4 through IMG-9 (list grid, Clause Library grid with risk colours, New Template editor, New Clause editor, Version History) against a locally mocked backend shows a close visual match on layout, column order, copy, colours and button placement.

pr.title: Add Template & Clause Library screen (UC3)
pr.body: Implements TemplateClauseLibraryPage and its owned components (TemplatesTab, ClauseLibraryTab, TemplateEditor, ClauseEditor, VersionHistoryModal), wired to the templates/clauses endpoints via a new clausesService and extended templatesService, the templateLibrarySlice store, and twelve hooks. Covers UC3's mandatory-field validation, predefined-list merge field insertion, Category/Risk Level dropdowns, Risk Level colour coding, Mandatory lock-in warning, Version History, Deactivate/Reactivate with confirmation, and role-gated access/management. See blockers for several story-vs-story and story-vs-design contradictions that were resolved using the endpoint role contract, plus a couple of inferred fields/UI.

blockers: BR-004 says Contract Owner should see this screen's fields read-only, while BR-009 and BR-010 say Contract Owner/Approver/External Party/Signer must be denied direct navigation to this exact screen entirely. These two stories directly contradict each other for Contract Owner. I resolved it by denying the whole screen (in-place 'You do not have permission to access this screen.' message, not a redirect, per AF-002's literal wording) to every role except Tenant Admin and Legal Reviewer, since BR-009 names this screen specifically ('outside of the UC2 selection flow') and the module's own GET /api/v1/templates and GET /api/v1/clauses endpoints already serve Contract Owner's read-only template/clause viewing inside the UC2 New Contract flow (owned by a different task), making a second read-only path into this exact screen redundant.

BR-004/BR-007/BR-012 say Legal Reviewer can see and click Deactivate/Reactivate; BR-008 explicitly says Legal Reviewer must not have a Deactivate option, and BR-012's own notes_assumptions flags this as an unresolved contradiction in the source document. I resolved it using the endpoint role contract, which is unambiguous: POST /api/v1/templates/{id}/deactivate, /reactivate and the clause equivalents all list roles: ['TENANT_ADMIN'] only. Deactivate/Reactivate buttons are therefore hidden for Legal Reviewer; Save/New Template/New Clause remain visible to both Tenant Admin and Legal Reviewer per BR-004/BR-008.

AF-005 ('Reject Unsupported Template File Format on Upload') describes a file-upload flow, but no template-file-upload endpoint or file-id field exists anywhere in this module's contract (TemplateResponse/CreateTemplateRequest have no fileId, and no /templates/.../upload path is listed) — unlike the separate third-party-paper upload in UC2, which is a different feature. I implemented Document Format as a plain PDF/DOCX dropdown (TemplateEditor.jsx), which inherently satisfies 'only PDF or DOCX selectable' without inventing an upload endpoint.

Template Category options are not enumerated as a DTO/enum anywhere in the contract. The New Template design screenshot (IMG-6) shows a helper line 'Sales Agreement, NDA, Procurement Contract, Service Agreement' under the Template Category field, which I used as the predefined dropdown list (TemplateEditor.jsx TEMPLATE_CATEGORIES). Clause Category and Risk Level option lists are explicitly enumerated in UC3-FV-002's acceptance criteria (Confidentiality/Liability/Termination/Payment Terms; Low/Medium/High) and I used those verbatim. Note the list grid design screenshots (IMG-4/5) show different, inconsistent sample category values (e.g. 'Commercial Contracts', 'Risk & Liability') — I treated those as non-canonical mock data and followed the story/helper-text-enumerated lists instead, per 'story wins over design' when they disagree.

Merge field predefined list ({Counterparty Name}, {Contract Value}, {Start Date}) is only given as an example in BR-006's notes_assumptions ('e.g.'), not as an exhaustive DTO-backed list, but it matches exactly what IMG-6's design shows as quick-insert chips, so I treated it as the actual predefined list (TemplateEditor.jsx MERGE_FIELDS) rather than inventing additional fields.

IMG-8 ('Existing Clauses in this Category' panel with a 'View all' link) is not one of this task's owned components and has no dedicated endpoint — it is rendered inline as part of ClauseEditor, derived client-side by filtering the already-loaded ClauseListResponse to the selected clause's category (no new network call, no new DTO fields). The 'View all' link from the design was omitted since it has no defined destination in this task's scope.

AF-006's optimistic-concurrency conflict message ('This clause/template was updated by another user...') relies entirely on the backend's own non-2xx `error` text (CLAUDE.md: 'show error to the user'), since neither UpdateTemplateRequest nor UpdateClauseRequest carries a version/timestamp field for the client to send back for comparison — there is nothing in the DTO to diff against client-side, so no client-side conflict pre-check exists, only surfacing of whatever the server rejects the PUT with.

AF-003 / BR-001's 'Remove Clause' button disabling for Mandatory clauses lives in the UC2 Contract Builder UI (a different page/task), not on this screen. This page's only responsibility toward that rule is correctly capturing and persisting the Mandatory checkbox and displaying it in the Clause Library grid and editor, which it does.

No field or endpoint indicates ahead of time whether a template/clause is attached to an active, unexecuted contract (AF-004/BR-003's pre-emptive 'Deactivate button disabled' state). The Deactivate button is therefore always enabled when Status is Active and canDeactivate is true; a blocked deactivation is surfaced only after the click, via the error banner showing the backend's rejection message, rather than being greyed out in advance.

Routed the page at /settings/template-clause-library since the module contract defines no explicit URL for this screen (only the breadcrumb 'Home Page / CLM Hub / Settings / Admin / Template & Clause Library' in the design); 'Settings / Admin' was folded into one breadcrumb segment and 'CLM Hub' was omitted as it refers to chrome owned by a different module/task.

Visual verification was done against a temporary, non-committed local mock HTTP server (not part of the repo) standing in for the real backend, since no backend is available in this environment; the real app still fails loudly at startup without VITE_API_BASE_URL per CLAUDE.md, and no mock/dev-fallback code was added to the committed source.
